instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Use only the English section of the Wiktionary entry
criteria.description: Full credit if all reported details are taken from the English section of the supplied Wiktionary entry for “algorithm”, or if the agent explicitly states it could not access/locate the English section due to page access issues or missing content. Partial credit if most items are from English but one or more appear to come from other language sections. No credit if the agent primarily uses non-English sections or external sources despite English-section content being accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the “English” heading with Etymology and Pronunciation content under it. Screenshot 2 shows the English “Noun” section with the headword line. Latest relevant is Screenshot 2 for noun details; Screenshot 1 for etymology/pronunciation.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: All extracted items in the predicted output correspond to content shown under the English section headings in the screenshots; no indication of using other language sections or external sources.

The visible content is clearly within the English section (the “English” header is shown), and the items the agent reported (etymology and pronunciation/hyphenation) are shown under that English section in the screenshot. There’s no visible non-English language section content being used.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy apparent for sourcing: the screenshot confirms the English section is the context for the etymology/pro­nunciation shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Wiktionary page section with the left sidebar table of contents including “English” and subsections like “Alternative forms”, “Etymology”, “Pronunciation”, and “Noun”. evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: What’s visible supports that the agent is working within the English section: the sidebar shows “English” expanded and the displayed content is the English “Noun” entry. However, the screenshot does not display the “Etymology” prose text or the “Pronunciation” section itself—only their links in the sidebar—so the specific etymology and IPA details in the agent’s predicted output cannot be verified from this screenshot alone. Still, nothing visible suggests the agent used a non-English section.

No direct contradiction is visible, just lack of on-screen support for those particular items.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM evidence confirms the extracted pronunciation, hyphenation, and noun-line information is within the English section. However, the prose etymology text and its four source-language stages are not present in the provided visible DOM content, so the claimed etymology stages cannot be verified as coming from the English section based on this DOM snapshot alone.

criteria.criterion: Report the four prose-etymology source-language stages (Middle English back to Arabic)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent reports exactly the four named source-language stages stated in the English prose etymology, spanning Middle English back to Arabic, matching wording and order as shown. Also award full credit if the agent clearly reports that fewer than four stages are present in the prose etymology or that the page/English etymology could not be accessed. Partial credit if fewer than four stages are reported when four are present, if order is wrong, or if the agent mixes in non-prose/tree details but still captures some correct stages. No credit if stages are invented or clearly not from the English prose etymology.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1’s Etymology prose visibly gives a chain: “From Middle English …, from Anglo-Norman …, from Medieval Latin …, from Arabic … (al-kawārizmiyy) …”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The four stages (Middle English → Anglo-Norman → Medieval Latin → Arabic) and their order match Screenshot 1. However, the predicted output’s Arabic transliteration uses “al-ḵawārizmiyy” while the screenshot shows “(al-kawārizmiyy)”; also the exact Arabic-script spelling in the screenshot is not clearly legible to confirm the precise diacritics. This is a transcription-accuracy issue within the 4 stages, so slight deduction.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the “Etymology” prose paragraph, the screenshot visibly contains: “From Middle English algorisme, augrym, from Anglo-Norman algorisme, augrim, from Medieval Latin algorismus, from Arabic … (al-kawārizmiyy), …”. The Arabic script is present but not fully legible in the screenshot; the transliteration “(al-kawārizmiyy)” is visible. The sentence continues with discussion of “Muhammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī” and Greek “ἀριθμός (arithmós)”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Largely satisfied. The screenshot supports the four stages and their order: Middle English → Anglo-Norman → Medieval Latin → Arabic. However, the agent’s predicted output gives the Arabic form as “الخَوَارِزْمِيّ (al-ḵawārizmiyy)”. The screenshot’s transliteration appears as “(al-kawārizmiyy)” (with k, not ḵ), and the exact Arabic-script string is not clearly readable here, so the agent’s exact Arabic spelling and diacritic “ḵ” are not confirmed by the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output: “(al-ḵawārizmiyy)” and Arabic “الخَوَارِزْمِيّ”. Screenshot shows “(al-kawārizmiyy)” and the Arabic script is present but not clearly legible to verify it matches the agent’s exact Arabic characters/diacritics.

dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The four reported source-language stages match exactly what is shown in the English prose etymology in DOM state 0, in correct order (Middle English → Anglo-Norman → Medieval Latin → Arabic). Full credit is warranted.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None; exactly four source-language stages (Middle English → Anglo-Norman → Medieval Latin → Arabic) are explicitly present in the prose etymology and match the reported sequence.

criteria.criterion: Provide the first IPA transcription and the Standard Southern British IPA transcription (distinct)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent reports (1) the first IPA transcription shown in the English pronunciation section and (2) the Standard Southern British IPA transcription, keeping them distinct and preserving IPA symbols exactly as displayed. Also award full credit if the agent explicitly states that one or both transcriptions are not present/visible in the English entry or the page could not be accessed. Partial credit if only one is given when both are present, if the two are conflated, or if minor transcription errors occur. No credit if pronunciations are missing without explanation or clearly not from the entry.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows first “IPA (key): /ˈælɡəɹɪðm̩/” and separately “(Standard Southern British) IPA (key): /ˈalɡəɹɪð(ə)m/”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Both requested IPA transcriptions are present in Screenshot 1 and are reproduced distinctly and exactly in the predicted output.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Satisfied. The agent’s first IPA transcription “/ˈælɡəɹɪðm̩/” matches the screenshot’s first IPA. The Standard Southern British IPA “/ˈalɡəɹɪð(ə)m/” also matches what is visible, and the two are kept distinct.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancies for the two requested IPA transcriptions; both appear to match the screenshot.

criteria.criterion: Report noun countability label(s) and plural form
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent reproduces the countability label(s) (e.g., countable/uncountable wording) exactly as displayed in the English entry and provides the plural form exactly as shown, or if the agent explicitly states that countability/plural information is not present/visible or the page could not be accessed. Partial credit if one of the two is missing when both are present, or if wording is paraphrased rather than exact but the intended label is clear. No credit if both are missing without explanation or incorrect.

criteria.criterion: Stopping condition respected (no extra, unrequested content)
criteria.description: Full credit if the agent stops after the requested items (four etymology stages, two labeled pronunciations, both hyphenations, countability label(s), and plural) without adding unrelated definitions/examples/extra pronunciations. Partial credit if minor additional content is included but the requested items are clearly present and easy to identify. No credit if substantial unrelated content is added that significantly exceeds scope or obscures the requested items.
